holdRule: max(3 s, words / 2.5 + 0.5 s, 1 s per 4 new lines on screen), at most 12 s; the words part is holdSeconds, the lines part is measured when the step runs

steps.text: Two identical customers at a mock bank use the same bill pay agent. One shares a password, the other approves a grant.
With the password, the bank sees the customer. With the grant, it sees the agent and holds it to the customer's limits.
A normal water bill gets paid both ways, and the grant adds no step for the customer.
Next, an invoice carries a hidden instruction, scripted for this demo, to pay a different account.
With the password, the money goes. With the grant, the bank refuses, because that account isn't an approved payee.
Now the customer wants the bill pay agent gone. A new password signs out both agents and the customer.
With the grant, the bank revokes that one agent, and everything else keeps working.
Then the customer disputes the water payment. The password leaves a login; the grant leaves a signed record naming the agent.
Last, every OpenA2A service is blocked. The bank still makes the same four decisions, with no outbound connections.
In this demo, the bank blocks unauthorized actions, including those triggered by prompt injection, because it checks each payment itself.
If you run security at a bank or credit union, write to the address on screen.
The bank is fictional and the scenarios are scripted. Open items, like proof of possession, are labeled on screen.
